subject: Tail-latency smoke + acceptance criteria for ApexData onboarding
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@apexdata.com>, Tom Richey <tom@apexdata.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-08T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Tail-latency smoke + acceptance criteria for ApexData onboarding

Hi Alyssa / Tom —

Thanks again for the run-through yesterday. To keep the onboarding window tight, proposed plan below for the acceptance testing we discussed. This is focused on the mixed production-like traffic you described (short chat prompts + long form generation bursts).

Summary of goals (what we'll certify):
- Latency: p50/p95/p99 measured at token-level and request-level for both short (<=64 tokens) and long (>=512 tokens) sessions.
- Throughput: sustained token throughput target per model instance and aggregate across the pool during 1hr steady-state.
- Error budget: <0.5% request errors, no 5xx spikes during ramp.
- Cold starts: measure tail latency impact during a cold-scale event (10% of pool recycled).

Proposed acceptance thresholds (prelim — please confirm):
- Short requests (<=64 tokens): p95 <= 120 ms, p99 <= 300 ms
- Long requests (>=512 tokens): p95 <= 450 ms, p99 <= 1.2 s
- Aggregate throughput: >= 2,000 tokens/sec sustained across the dedicated pool during steady-state
- KV cache hit rate target: >= 70% for prefix-heavy workloads

Planned test stages (timeline):
1) Smoke (30m) — basic correctness, endpoints, auth, payload shapes.
2) Warmup ramp (20m) — gradual increase to steady-state to populate caches.
3) Steady-state run (60m) — constant arrival pattern matching your traffic mix.
4) Stress probes (2x for 15m) — short bursts to verify graceful degradation & fallback routing.
5) Cold-scale test (10m) — kill 10% of nodes to measure cold-start tail latency.

Artifacts we'll provide after each stage: k6 load logs, aggregated token latency CSV, Grafana dashboards snapshot, raw error logs. I've attached the initial k6 configuration we plan to run.

Can you confirm the thresholds above and the time windows that work for your ops team? Also confirm the origin IPs from which your load agents will run (we'll whitelist in advance).

Thanks —
Karthik Iyer
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
karthik@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0147

From: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@apexdata.com>

Date: 2027-10-09T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tail-latency smoke + acceptance criteria for ApexData onboarding

Thanks Karthik — this looks mostly aligned. A few clarifications from our side: 

- Our production mix is roughly 65% short prompts (<=64 tokens), 30% medium (65-256), 5% long (>=512) but the long ones are the key failure mode.
- Target SLA from procurement: p95 <= 150ms for short, p99 <= 500ms for long. We can accept your suggested p95/p99 for long if you can show consistent p99 < 1s in the cold-scale test.
- Aggregate throughput: our peak is closer to 3,200 tokens/sec for the region. Can Redwood demonstrate >=3k tokens/sec sustained? If needed we can carve a higher dedicated pool under the committed capacity.

We will run agents from two locations: us-west-2 (34.210.45.22) and us-east-1 (3.86.120.11). Please confirm whitelisting windows.

Also, we'll need the CSV results in a pinned Drive folder and a short one-page signoff doc for procurement after acceptance.

Alyssa Chen
Head of Platform Engineering, ApexData
alyssa@apexdata.com

P.S. cc'ing Tom to make sure this syncs with their traffic ops schedule.
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
To: Alyssa Chen <alyssa@apexdata.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: 2027-10-10T08:57:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Tail-latency smoke + acceptance criteria for ApexData onboarding

Great notes — I updated the test plan and attachments based on the higher throughput ask. Key operational notes below: 

- Pool sizing: we'll provision a 12-GPU dedicated pool for the run (planned), which we estimate will sustain ~3.2k tokens/sec with current quantization profile. If we see headroom issues we'll spin an extra 3 GPUs for the stress probes.
- Measurement details: token-level latencies recorded client-side and server-side. We'll calculate per-request end-to-end latency (client submit -> final token emitted). We'll also report per-token generation latency to identify decoder stalls.
- Warmup: 30 minutes to reach cache steady-state given your prefix reuse patterns.
- Metrics we'll export:
  * latency-p50/p95/p99 by short/medium/long buckets (CSV)
  * tokens-per-second overall and per-model-shard
  * error counts and stack traces for any 5xx
  * cache hit/miss rates and average KV retrieval time

Attached: updated k6-mixed-workload-config.json (adds long-prompt templates), plus the redwood_sla_matrix_v2.xlsx that maps test results to acceptance pass/fail logic.

Please confirm the run window: 2027-10-11 09:00-12:00 PDT. We'll snapshot Grafana urls during the run and drop links into the Drive folder.

—Ben
Ben Carter
Onboarding Lead, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Tail-latency smoke + acceptance criteria for ApexData onboarding

Forwarding final artifacts and short summary from today's run (results attached).

Quick summary:
- Steady-state (60m) observed: aggregate 3,060 tokens/sec; short-request p95=138ms (within procurement threshold), long-request p95=410ms, long-request p99=980ms.
- Cold-scale probe: p99 spike to 1.15s for a 2-minute window immediately after node recycle, which exceeds the ideal 1s target but behavior matched expected cold-start curve; we captured full traces.
- Error rate: 0.28% request errors (all were transient rate-limit returns from a single agent; we re-ran the agent and results cleared).
- KV cache hit rate: 73% during steady-state.

Artifacts included in Drive folder: apex_results_summary_20271011.csv (aggregated metrics), k6-mixed-workload-config.json (script & load spec), grafana_snapshot_20271011.png, raw_error_traces.tar.gz, redwood_sla_matrix_v2.xlsx (pass/fail logic).

Next steps:
1) I will upload the one-page signoff doc for procurement once you confirm acceptance criteria gating (particularly how you prefer to treat the cold-scale p99 spike).
2) If you want us to re-run the cold-scale test with a slightly higher pre-warm or additional nodes to reduce tail, we can schedule a 2-hour slot next week.

Please let me know if ApexData accepts these results for the onboarding milestone or if you'd like an additional verification run.

Thanks —
Karthik
